english: Say also that clear-voiced Neaera hasten
problem: argutae Neaerae is dative (the person told), not the subject of a that-clause; the English makes Neaera a nominative. Sense survives.
suggested: Tell also clear-voiced Neaera that she should hasten

english: Streams of pure water and a wood of acres
problem: rivos is the old spelling of nominative singular rivus (as laevos = laevus in 3.27.15), one of the singular subjects of fallit on line 32; 'Streams' makes it plural.
suggested: A stream of pure water and a wood of acres

problem: sorte is ablative of respect ('in lot') and beatior is predicative nominative agreeing with the subjects of lines 29-30 (stream, wood, faith of crop); fallit is singular. 'escape, a lot more blessed' turns sorte into a nominative noun, has a plural verb, and reads in English as 'much more blessed'. The note's 'my lot ... escapes his notice' repeats the misconstrual.
suggested: escapes his notice, more blessed in lot.

english: After a little you will flee the hard, un-bold
problem: inaudax is nominative with raptor (line 4), as the note says, but 'the hard, un-bold battles' attaches it to proelia in the English.
suggested: hard, after a little you will flee, un-bold,
